no completed academic work is to be discarded merely because its old number changes.

## FINAL COURSE RESOURCE ARCHITECTURE The Master Course Map defines where each subtopic belongs. The actual course workspace defines what is attached to it. 200L → Physiology → Topic → Subtopic Each subtopic should be treated as a complete learning unit with these resource layers: - 📖 Notes - ❓ MCQs - 🔄 Flashcards - 📄 Past Papers - 🩺 Clinical Vignettes - 🖼️ Visuals / Diagrams / Graphs - 🧠 Clinical Correlations - 🧪 Practical / Laboratory - ✍️ Theory / SAQs + Model Answers - 📊 Calculations / Data Interpretation where applicable - 🎯 High-Yield / Revision - 📚 Sources / References / Attribution ### Example 200L → Physiology → Topic 4: Cardiovascular Physiology → 4.7 Cardiac Cycle

→ Notes

→ MCQs

→ Flashcards

→ Past Papers

→ Clinical Vignettes

→ Visuals

→ Clinical Correlations

→ Practical

→ Theory / SAQs

→ Calculations / Data Interpretation

→ High-Yield / Revision

→ Sources Rule: Do not create separate disconnected resource systems that lose the Topic/Subtopic relationship. Every resource must remain traceable to its exact 200L course, topic and subtopic. ## INFINITE QUESTION-BANK / RESOURCE-SOURCING STRATEGY ### Core principle After the Notes layer is sufficiently complete, the downstream learning resources should be built from a broad Nigerian medical-education source pool, not from a single university or a single question set. Priority source pool includes publicly available curricula, course outlines, lecture objectives, practical guides, departmental materials and assessment patterns from Nigerian universities. Examples already verified include Bayero University, University of Medical Sciences Ondo, Federal University Oye-Ekiti, Olabisi Onabanjo University, State University of Medical and Applied Sciences, and other Nigerian institutions where relevant. ### Question-bank objective Build an extremely large, high-quality question bank so that the learner—not the content author—controls the size of each study session. The app should eventually support: - User-selected number of questions - Topic/subtopic filtering - Course filtering - Difficulty filtering - Question-type filtering - Randomized selection - No-repeat exposure until the available pool has been exhausted, where technically feasible - Persistent question history so previously seen questions can be tracked - Multiple attempts without recycling the same questions unnecessarily - Weak-area targeting - Fresh mixed-question sessions - Progressive difficulty ### Source integrity Do NOT copy large blocks of copyrighted university examination papers or lecture materials verbatim. Use legitimate/publicly available material to identify tested concepts, learning objectives, question styles and curriculum coverage, then create original, academically equivalent questions and explanations. Past-paper questions may be linked/referenced where legitimately available, but the internal generated bank should be original, transformed and traceable to its learning objective/source concept. ### Resource layers after Notes For each relevant subtopic, progressively build: Notes → Visuals → Clinical Correlations/Vignettes → Flashcards → MCQs → Past Papers → Theory/SAQs → Practical/Data Interpretation → High-Yield Revision Not every layer must exist identically for every subtopic; use academic judgment. For example, quantitative physiology should receive substantially more calculations/data interpretation, while anatomy should receive substantially more labelled visuals/practical identification. ### Nigerian-source diversity The goal is not to imitate one university. Cross-check Nigerian curricula and teaching emphasis to identify: - Commonly taught concepts - University-specific emphasis - Recurring examination themes - Practical competencies - Terminology differences - Areas commonly tested across institutions Then synthesize these into a broader TheMedConfidant bank. ### Current verification examples Bayero University's published MBBS/BDS physiology structure includes General Principles and Cell Physiology, Excitable Tissues, Autonomic Nervous System, Blood and Immunity, Cardiovascular System, practical physiology, then Respiratory, Renal, Metabolism/Skin, Gastrointestinal, Liver/Biliary, Endocrine and Reproductive physiology. citeturn0search0turn0search3 UNIMED's 200L MBBS structure includes Gross Anatomy, Histology, Embryology, General Biochemistry, Introductory/General Physiology, Blood and Body Fluid, Excitable Tissue/Contractile Cells/CNS/ANS, then GI, Respiratory and Cardiovascular Physiology. citeturn0search1 FUOYE and other Nigerian institutions similarly show 200L physiology alongside anatomy and biochemistry, reinforcing the need for a cross-university rather than single-school architecture. citeturn0search11turn0search9 This source-diversity rule applies to the whole 200L build, not just Physiology. ## 200L PHYSIOLOGY — NORMALIZED CURRICULUM MAP (WORKING MASTER) ### TOPIC 1 — General tracings and data interpretation 14.19 Experimental error and data handling 14.20 Integrated clinical reasoning ## RESOURCE LAYERS — EVERY SUBTOPIC Each numbered subtopic is a hub for: Notes → Visuals → Clinical Correlations → Clinical Vignettes → Flashcards → MCQs → Past Papers → Theory/SAQs → Practical/Laboratory → Calculations/Data Interpretation → High-Yield/Revision → Sources/Attribution. ## LEGACY MIGRATION RULE Existing flat-numbered pages (including the previously built 1–118+ and later extension pages) are source material, not final numbering. They must be mapped into the normalized Topic/Subtopic structure and retained; do not delete or duplicate them unnecessarily. Where an existing page combines multiple concepts, split its content conceptually across the relevant subtopics rather than forcing the old number into the new system. ## QUESTION-BANK PRINCIPLE After notes are stable, assessment resources should be sourced/triangulated against Bowen first, then broader Nigerian university curricula and assessment patterns. Genuine past-paper material must remain clearly identified as such; original questions should be generated from the verified learning objectives and assessment patterns. The eventual bank should be deliberately very large so the learner can select a session size while the engine minimizes unnecessary repetition. ## 🔥 CURRENT BUILD STATUS — 30 AUG 2026 Strategy: Bowen-first preclinical build. Existing legacy physiology material is being reorganized into the new Topic → Subtopic architecture; no unnecessary rewriting. ### Production pipeline Curriculum audit → Notes → Visuals → Clinical correlations/vignettes → Flashcards → Massive MCQ bank → Past papers → Theory/SAQs → Practical/data interpretation → High-yield/revision → QA ### Assessment-bank principle The question bank is intentionally vast, not capped at an arbitrary number per subtopic. Questions will be sourced/derived from Bowen assessment patterns first, then triangulated against Nigerian university curricula and publicly available educational/assessment material. Genuine past-paper questions remain clearly identified; original questions are generated from the same tested concepts rather than misrepresented as past papers. ### Anti-repeat objective The eventual quiz engine should draw from the largest feasible pool, track questions already served to the learner, minimize repeats, and allow the learner to choose a session size/topic/difficulty. Repetition should be used deliberately for weak-area reinforcement, not because the bank is small. ### Scope discipline Current scope is preclinical 100L + 200L. Multi-university support is a later mapping layer; 300L+ and clinical-year content are not current production targets. ### Architecture target 200L → Course → Topic → Subtopic → resource ecosystem Every course should have its own resource hubs (Notes, MCQs, Flashcards, Past Papers, etc.), while each subtopic remains traceable to its exact course/topic/subtopic. ## CLEANUP STATUS — 30 AUG 2026 Active navigation uses the final hierarchy: 200L → Physiology → Topic → Subtopic. Legacy numbered pages are source/archive material only and must not appear as active navigation entries.

resources.title: 2️⃣ 200L — Legacy / Previous Structure
resources.content: ## DESIGN RULES — LOCKED Structure according to function. Simplicity over complexity. - One course page = one clear entry point. - One resource should live where the learner expects to find it. - Do not create separate layers merely because they are technically possible. - Notes own the academic hierarchy: Topic → Subtopic → explanation + relevant visuals. - Flashcards are for recall; images are included when they improve recognition or understanding. - MCQs are for testing and can be filtered by topic, difficulty and university. - Past Papers are organised for retrieval, not duplicated across every topic. - Clinical Vignettes connect knowledge to clinical reasoning. - Resources collect legitimate PDFs, links, videos and research without cluttering the Notes. - Progress shows what the learner has actually studied/mastered. If a feature does not have a clear learner-facing function, it does not get its own section. ### The simple learner journey Course → Choose what you want to do → Study / Practise / Review That is the architecture we build from here. ## 🧭 NEW 200L COURSE ARCHITECTURE — REBUILD This is the clean starting backbone for the 200L medical-study library. Primary courses: - 🫀 Physiology - 🦴 Anatomy - 🧪 Biochemistry Each course opens into the same resource architecture: Notes → Flashcards → MCQs → Past Papers → Clinical Vignettes → Practicals → Research Papers → Resources/PDFs → Video/External Learning → Revision & Progress. Topics and subtopics will be built inside Notes under each course, rather than creating a separate visual hierarchy. Visual rule: every appropriate note/subtopic and every image-capable flashcard set receives relevant educational visuals. OpenStax/public-domain/open-license sources will be used where suitable, with attribution/licensing preserved. Past-paper rule: later, papers can be organised by University → Course → Year/Exam, with a selected-university filter for the learner. This section is the new active backbone. Legacy material elsewhere is not part of the navigation. Status: Foundation phase Owner: Bablo ™ Scope: Bowen University medical/preclinical content ## Working scope 200L will be developed as a source-grounded, visually rich learning library rather than a question-generation exercise. ### Initial disciplines - Anatomy - Physiology - Biochemistry - Associated practical/tutorial material where it belongs to the verified Bowen curriculum ## Production standard For each verified topic: - Original, source-grounded Notes - Visual layer identified and sourced/licensed appropriately - ≥50 genuinely useful Flashcards - ≥50 genuinely useful MCQs - As much as possible or all available theory/short-answer questions with model answers - Bloom's Taxonomy tagging - Pareto yield tagging - Difficulty tagging - Calculation verification where applicable - Clinical/application connections where appropriate - No duplicated or filler questions ## Source hierarchy 1. Legitimately available student/reference materials 2. Reputable academic/medical references for cross-checking 3. Open/licensed visual sources such as OpenStax and appropriate public-domain/open-access collections 4. Original TheMedConfidant explanations, diagrams, learning aids and questions ## Curriculum verification Bowen-specific course codes and topic sequence must be verified before mass content production. Public Bowen teaching-timetable evidence already confirms 200L MBBS teaching in Gross Anatomy, Embryology, Physiology, Physiology Practical and Biochemistry, with examples including ANA 201 and PHS/BCH-labelled teaching. This is evidence for the discipline structure, not yet a complete authoritative course outline. ## Build sequence 1. Verify Bowen 200L curriculum/course codes 2. Audit available 200L source material 3. Create course-level Notion structure 4. Build one complete topic as the quality benchmark 5. Scale topic-by-topic ## Visual-first principle Visuals are part of the learning architecture. Anatomy should use labelled/spatial diagrams and histology imagery where appropriate; Physiology should use graphs, mechanisms and flow diagrams; Biochemistry should use pathway, molecular and reaction visuals. The app should ultimately support visual, text-based and audiovisual learning without turning the notes into textbook scans. ## Important boundary Claude owns the 100L content lane. This 200L branch is developed independently and should not overwrite or restructure Claude's 100L work. 📋 Bowen 200L — Verified Curriculum & Build Map Physiology 200L — Strategic Architecture & Resource Map 📚 200L Physiology — Master Course Map Topic 6 — Renal Physiology ### ACTIVE COURSE BACKBONES The three course pages below are the new entry points for 200L. Each course owns its own Notes, Flashcards, MCQs, Past Papers, Clinical Vignettes, Practicals, Research Papers, Resources/PDFs, Video/External Learning, and Revision/Progress layers. Course entry points to build: - 🫀 Physiology - 🦴 Anatomy - 🧪 Biochemistry ### Resource architecture (same across all three courses) 1. 📖 Notes 2. 🧠 Flashcards — image-rich where the concept benefits from visual recall 3. 📝 MCQs — topic, difficulty, Bloom level and university filters later 4. 📄 Past Papers — university → course → year/exam 5. 🩺 Clinical Vignettes 6. 🔬 Practicals / Lab & Dissection / Calculations, where applicable 7. 🧬 Research Papers & Evidence 8. 📚 Recommended Textbooks / Reading Lists 9. 📥 Downloadable PDFs & Open-access Resources 10. 🎥 Videos / Lectures / External Learning Links 11. 📊 Revision, Weak Areas & Progress 12. ⚡ Rapid Review / High-Yield Sheets Important: these are resource layers. The actual academic hierarchy remains Course → Notes → Topic → Subtopic. Visuals belong inside the relevant note/subtopic and inside appropriate flashcards—not as a separate course hierarchy. --- BUILD ORDER: Course backbones first → resource sections → Notes topics/subtopics → visuals embedded at subtopic level → question/flashcard layers → university past papers and evidence/resource library. Structural rule locked: no standalone "Visual Layer" pages for active navigation. Visual assets are embedded/placed within the note or subtopic they teach. ### 🫀 PHYSIOLOGY Course backbone: Notes, Flashcards, MCQs, Past Papers, Clinical Vignettes, Practicals, Research Papers, Resources/PDFs, Videos, Rapid Review, Revision & Progress. ### 🦴 ANATOMY Course backbone: Notes, Flashcards, MCQs, Past Papers, Clinical Vignettes, Dissection/Practical, Research Papers, Resources/PDFs, Videos, Rapid Review, Revision & Progress. ### 🧪 BIOCHEMISTRY Course backbone: Notes, Flashcards, MCQs, Past Papers, Clinical Vignettes, Practical/Calculations, Research Papers, Resources/PDFs, Videos, Rapid Review, Revision & Progress.

resources.title: 🧭 200L — Strategic Architecture & Resource Map
resources.content: ## Strategic objective Build Bowen 200L as a source-grounded, visually rich preclinical library that can later power TheMedConfidant's app. ## Current verified direction Bowen's public College of Health Sciences identifies Medicine and Surgery as an MBBS programme. Recent Bowen timetable material shows 200L teaching activity involving Anatomy and Physiology, including anatomy dissection and physiology practical work. Public timetable evidence is useful for triangulation, but exact current MBBS course codes and topic sequence remain subject to confirmation from current student/department material. ## 200L lanes ### Anatomy - Gross anatomy - Embryology - Histology - Dissection/practical anatomy ### Physiology - Systems physiology - Cardiovascular physiology - Respiratory physiology - Renal physiology - Gastrointestinal physiology - Endocrine physiology - Neurophysiology - Physiology practicals ### Biochemistry - Molecular biochemistry - Metabolism - Enzymology/regulation - Clinical correlations - Practical/tutorial work where applicable ## Resource strategy ### Tier 1 — student's legitimate academic materials Use supplied lecture notes, course outlines, permitted textbooks and past papers as the primary grounding layer when available. ### Tier 2 — cross-checking Use reputable medical/academic sources to verify important mechanisms, terminology and calculations. ### Tier 3 — visual/reference layer Prioritize OpenStax, NLM/NIH/public-domain resources, Wikimedia Commons files with individually verified licences, and other openly licensed resources. ### Tier 4 — original TheMedConfidant layer Create original explanations, diagrams, flowcharts, mnemonics, tables, flashcards and questions. ## Visual architecture For each topic, define visuals before finalizing the note: - Anatomy: orientation, labelled structures, relationships, histology, dissection views - Physiology: mechanisms, graphs, pressure/volume relationships, cycles, flow diagrams, ECG/other tracings where relevant - Biochemistry: pathways, molecular structures, reaction maps, regulation diagrams Each external visual should have a source/licence record. Do not use textbook scans or assume an entire repository has one universal licence. ## Quality gate per topic 1. Source map complete 2. Learning objectives defined 3. Original note written and verified 4. Visual plan completed 5. ≥50 useful flashcards 6. ≥50 genuine MCQs 7. 5–6 theory/short-answer questions with model answers 8. Bloom/Pareto/difficulty tags applied 9. Calculations independently checked 10. Duplicate/filler audit ## First benchmark candidate Physiology — Cardiovascular System Reason: it can test the complete learning architecture using text, diagrams, graphs, mechanisms, clinical application, flashcards, MCQs and theory questions. ## Important boundary Claude owns the 100L lane. This page and all subsequent 200L work are independent and should not modify Claude's 100L content.
